caption: One repeater set to 1: the signal comes out 2 ticks later. Each repeater adds 2 ticks per notch of its setting, so any even delay is a line of them, 2 blocks (repeater + stone) per started 8 ticks (track delay, family delay-rep2: N = 2 + 8n gt, n = 0)

One repeater set to 2: the signal comes out 4 ticks later; a pulse shorter than 4 ticks comes out stretched to 4 (a line of repeaters set to 1 keeps it, at 2 blocks per 2 ticks). Each repeater adds 2 ticks per notch of its setting, so any even delay is a line of them, 2 blocks (repeater + stone) per started 8 ticks (track delay, family delay-rep4: N = 4 + 8n gt, n = 0)

Delay line, 7 ticks, 10 blocks: the odd delays a repeater line cannot make. Two stages of two sticky pistons with redstone blocks, joined by a repeater set to 1. In each stage the first piston pushes its block against the second piston, which pulls its own block away from the next part. A piston set off by a block ARRIVING acts one tick later than one set off by a signal, so each stage takes 3 ticks one way and 2 the other, and inverts; two stages in a row add up to the same odd number on both edges.
